classification.difficultyReason: Construct an array retaining repeated book types, then count favourable outcomes.

content.prompt: One bookshelf contains 3 storybooks and 1 textbook, while the next shelf holds 2 storybooks and 3 textbooks.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw an array showing the various ways in which you could pick a pair of books, one from each shelf.

inlines.text: S = storybook; T = textbook. Rows represent the first shelf; columns represent the second shelf.
S = storybook; T = textbook. Give each individual book its own row or column, even when its type repeats. The first entry in each pair is from the first shelf.

children.prompt: Use this array to find the probability that:

answer.worked:
There are 6 $(S,S)$ entries among the 20 equally likely outcomes.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{both storybooks})&=\frac{6}{20}\\P(\text{both storybooks})&=\frac{3}{10}\end{align*}$$

There are 3 $(T,T)$ entries among the 20 equally likely outcomes.
$$P(\text{both textbooks})=\frac{3}{20}.$$
